audit.why: EVEN at 5.5/10 and 52.38% over 147 games. Neither kit kills the other in a straight 1v1 — it is a CC-chicken standoff that cashes out in teamfights. The mirror audit (audits/top/galio__sejuani.json) reached the same verdict from Galio's side.
audit.corrected: Difficulty untouched; the reasons were made mechanical.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike and the late-game block treat Hero's Entrance as a permanent overhang with no cost, and neither ultimate carries a cooldown.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s at 4000/4750/5500 range; Glacial Prison is 120/105/90s at 1300. You get roughly three ultimates for every two of his, which is the actual shape of the spike and the reason banking R for objectives works.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into mid and late; the level-6 tilt is kept but priced.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors, both repeated. (a) 'Fury of the North's Permafrost resistances' and 'passive armor... shield stacks' — the page fuses Permafrost with the passive and invents stacks. (b) 'if you see him wind up the W channel, E Permafrost him out of the taunt immediately' — presented as an on-demand interrupt.
audit.why: Riot on Fury of the North: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows.' It is an out-of-combat buff, not a stacking shield, and Permafrost has nothing to do with it. Riot on Permafrost: 'Sejuani freezes and stuns an enemy champion that has maximum Frost stacks' — you cannot press it as a reaction. The stacks come from Winter's Wrath (9/8/7/6/5s) and autos, so the interrupt has to be pre-loaded before he starts charging Shield of Durand (18/17/16/15/14s), not fired in response to it.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor named correctly and described as armour, MR and slow immunity; Permafrost restated as requiring max Frost stacks, with the stacking done before his channel starts.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Justice Punch as matchup-defining and gives no number; 'Your Q dash' is unnamed and unpriced.
audit.why: Justice Punch 11/10/9/8/7s, 650 range; Arctic Assault 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s, 650 range. His engage comes back roughly twice as fast as yours — that asymmetry is the whole reason you do not spend Q first.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, phases[3].why and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page asserts that stunning Galio cancels the Shield of Durand taunt.
audit.why: Riot's text calls it a charge, not a channel, and the kit file's derived flags list no channel on W. Whether hard CC during the charge cancels the taunt outright, or merely delays the release, is not answerable from the kit data, and needsResearch is empty by design. The claim was removed rather than restated.
audit.corrected: Replaced with what the data does support: he moves slowly while charging, the charge is 18s at rank 1, and your stun has to be pre-loaded via Frost stacks.

audit.why: Nothing in the page is pinned to a patch-specific number, and the kit file is built on ddragon 16.15.1, matching the live 26.15 patch.

edits.after: At level 1 you have a passive edge — Fury of the North grants Frost Armor out of combat, armour, MR and immunity to slows, and his Winds of War pokes for little through it at 825 range while costing him mana. Take W, auto the wave, and let him spend mana on damage you eat for free. Do not walk into his auto range unprompted, because Colossal Smash empowers his next basic with bonus magic damage in an area, but the level-1 initiative is yours if you hold position and deny him the step-up. At level 2 the matchup flattens — Justice Punch is a 650 dash on 11 seconds at rank 1, so he can close the moment your W is down and the threat runs both ways. At level 3, respect Shield of Durand: 18 seconds at rank 1, he moves slowly while he charges it, and the release taunts and damages everything near him. Permafrost is not an interrupt you can press on demand — it only fires at maximum Frost stacks — so land both Winter's Wrath arcs before he starts charging, not after.
edits.before: At level 1 you actually have a passive edge — Fury of the North's Permafrost resistances activate before either of you has an ability that matters, and his Q Winds of War costs mana and pokes for low damage through your frost armor. Take W, auto the wave, and let him spend mana on poke you are eating for free. Do not step into his auto range unprompted because his passive Colossal Smash hits hard, but the level 1 initiative is yours if you hold position and deny him the step-up. At level 2 the matchup flattens — he gets Justice Punch and can now gap-close onto you if your W is down, so the threat goes both ways and neither side has a clean answer. At level 3 respect Shield of Durand hard: if you see him wind up the W channel, E Permafrost him out of the taunt immediately — stunning him cancels the taunt and denies the magic proc entirely. That interrupt is your whole level 3 trade pattern.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a genuine stalemate — his MR stacking blunts your magic damage, your Frost Armor blunts his Colossal Smash proc, and neither of you threatens a solo kill without a jungler. Farm with Winter's Wrath arcs on their 9-second cooldown so Frost stacks stay live, and watch Justice Punch: 11 seconds at rank 1, and the moment it is spent is your window to Arctic Assault forward and start the chain. Do not Q while Justice Punch is up — he knocks you up mid-charge and your 18-second engage dies on the spot. Level 6 tilts to him: Hero's Entrance is 180 seconds but reaches 4000 units at rank 1, so if your jungler arrives at the same moment Galio presses R, you have handed the enemy a 2v2 with his CC layered on top of yours. Before any committed engage at 6, check his R status and his mid laner's position, and only then consider Arctic Assault.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a genuine stalemate — his MR stacking blanks your frost damage, your resistances blunt his magic proc, and neither of you threatens a solo kill without a jungler. Farm the wave with W arcs to build Frost stacks passively and look for Justice Punch cooldowns: the second it lands or expires, that is the window to Q forward and start the Frost chain. Do not Q when Justice Punch is available — he knocks you up mid-charge and your engage dies on the spot. Level 6 is where the matchup tilts to him: Hero's Entrance is global, and if your jungler comes for a gank at the same moment Galio presses R mid, you have just handed the enemy a free 2v2 with his CC overlapping yours. Before any committed engage at 6, ping his R status, check the minimap for his mid laner's position, and only then consider your Arctic Assault.

edits.after: By 2+ items this is an even teamfight tank mirror decided by whose CC lands first on the enemy carry — a 1300-range Glacial Prison thrown before his Hero's Entrance hard-engages a fight he cannot rotate into, while his R landing first re-engages your engage and swings it back. Your ultimate is 120 seconds at rank 1 against his 180, so you simply get more of them: spend one on a river or pit fight with your team already behind you. Zone away from his taunt radius in skirmishes and never stand grouped in a tight brush cluster where Shield of Durand tags four people at once. One clean Glacial Prison is worth more than the entire laning phase, and he has no answer to your chain once both CC sets land on the same target.
edits.before: By 2+ items this is an even teamfight tank mirror decided entirely by whose CC chain lands first on the enemy carry — Glacial Prison cast before his Hero's Entrance means you hard-engage a fight he cannot rotate into fast enough; his R arriving first means he re-engages your engage and the fight swings the other way. Zone your Q and R away from his taunt radius in skirmishes and never stand grouped in a tight brush cluster where Shield of Durand tags four people at once. Your carry tool is a multi-man R into a river or pit with your team already behind you — one clean Glacial Prison is worth more than the entire laning phase combined, and he has no hard answer to your CC once both chains land simultaneously on the same target.

notes: Mirror: audits/top/galio__sejuani.json already exists and this proposal reuses its findings rather than re-deriving them — same Frost Armor correction, same Permafrost-is-1.5s-and-gated-on-stacks correction, same magic-damage typing, same verdict that the lane is an EVEN standoff. The two pages agree on the level chart as it already stands (Skill through First item, Sejuani at 2+ items, with inverse ratings), so no chart edits were needed. Galio's Justice Punch carries a derived 'terrain' flag that produced a 'Galio can cut your retreat' row in _missing-interactions.json for this matchup; Riot's text for the ability says only that he steps back, charges, and knocks up the first champion he meets — no terrain interaction — so the row was ignored, exactly as the mirror audit ignored it. Open question recorded under unverified: whether hard CC during the Shield of Durand charge cancels the taunt or only delays it.
